prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map clarifies the geometry of the dimly lit indoor living room and adjoining dining area across the five frames as the camera wearer pans their head from left to right (frames 1 to 3) and then back to the left (frames 4 to 5). In frames 1 and 5, a person stands in the left foreground roughly 1.5 to 2.5 metres away in front of a recessed dining-area window about 4 to 5 metres back, with their lower body cropped out at the bottom edge of the frame and nothing within arm's reach of the camera wearer except the nearby left wall (within 1 metre). In frames 2 through 4, as the view sweeps right and back left, the depth gradient reveals a dark sofa (about 2 to 3 metres away) below a four-pane window on the right wall, two armchairs further to the left in the corner (roughly 3 to 4 metres away and 1 to 2 metres from the sofa), a table lamp at the right end of the sofa (around 2 metres away, occluding the lower-right window pane), and a door on the far right in frame 3 (roughly 2.5 metres away). Compared to the underexposed RGB frames, the depth map makes the silhouettes and relative distances of the dark armchairs, sofa, and lamp much easier to distinguish against the shadowed walls. However, the depth map is unreliable on the bright window panes in frame 3 and the recessed opening in frames 1 and 5, where overexposed glass and backlighting cause abrupt dark depth dropouts, as well as along the bottom foreground of frames 3 and 4 where a diffuse bright band blurs the exact floor-to-furniture boundary.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only a few discrete regions across the panning sequence: a 'person' mask in the lower-left foreground of frames 1 and 5, and light-blue masks mislabelled as 'tv' in frames 2, 3, and 4. Using the RGB strip for context, the person in frames 1 and 5 is about 1.5 to 2.5 metres in front of the camera wearer, positioned to the left of the main living room corner and partially cut off below the waist by the bottom frame boundary, with their head and torso oriented roughly toward or slightly angled relative to the camera wearer (though heavy motion blur and backlighting obscure exact gaze). The regions labelled 'tv' actually correspond to the bright four-pane window on the right wall in frames 2 and 4 (roughly 2.5 to 3.5 metres away, above and behind the sofa) and solely the table lamp shade in front of the right window pane in frame 3 (about 2 metres away, within arm's reach of the sofa's right armrest). While the segmentation map cleanly separates the backlit person silhouette in frames 1 and 5 and the lamp shade in frame 3 from the dark surroundings, it is highly unreliable for overall scene understanding. It completely misses the sofa, armchairs, dining furniture, and door due to severe underexposure, while falsely classifying the backlit window panes and lamp shade as televisions.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely blank (all black) across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand keypoints in the sequence. From the RGB and depth context, a single person is present in frames 1 and 5 at a distance of roughly 1.5 to 2.5 metres to the lower left, standing in front of the distant dining-area window (4 to 5 metres away) and separated by about 2 to 3 metres from the living room chairs and sofa to the right. As the camera wearer turns their head right across frames 2 and 3—bringing the sofa, armchairs, lamp, and door into view at 2 to 4 metres distance—the person exits the left side of the field of view before reappearing in frame 5 when the wearer turns back left. Because the person is only visible from the chest up at the bottom edge of frames 1 and 5 and is heavily blurred and backlit against the window, neither the pose map nor the RGB image can reliably resolve their exact facial orientation, gaze direction, or hand positions, and no one is within arm's reach of the camera wearer. Consequently, the pose map offers no spatial information beyond what is visible in RGB and is unreliable under these motion-blurred, low-light conditions.
